notes_measurement: [regulatory] Verbatim: 'in the 53-week study, some necrotic non-neuronal cells and cellular debris were observed in one mid-dose male and in 3 of 7 high-dose males. notes_measurement: [regulatory] MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE. Verbatim: 'An investigational study was conducted in cynomolgus monkeys, which provided support that the hippocampal vacuoles contain nusinersen and do not represent an adverse histopathological finding. Indeed, the observation of vacuoles is linked to the method of tissue preservation in the presence of drug, thereby allowing these to be called fixation-induced vacuoles. Vacuolation in the inferior hippocampus was absent in tissues immersion-fixed in Carnoy's or perfusion-fixed with Karnovsky's fixative.' Doses not printed in the EPAR text -> dose TBD. This row materially discounts the vacuolation rows above. grade_provisional

notes_measurement: [regulatory] QUANTIFIED POST-MARKETING SIGNAL. Verbatim: 'Three cases of aseptic meningitis were reported (in children aged 3, 11 and 13) who experienced clinical signs and symptoms consistent with meningitis shortly after receiving nusinersen treatment. Routine bacterial cultures and viral polymerase chain reaction studies (reported in 2 cases) were negative... The events resolved without reported sequalae and treatment with nusinersen continued for all 3 children. Among a total of 439 person years of nusinersen exposure in the post-marketing setting, the 3 cases of meningitis reported is more than expected based on comparisons with children in the general population (6 to 70 cases per 100,000 among young children and 3 to 5 cases per 100,000 among older children).' CHMP concluded causality was 'a reasonable possibility'. Clinically significant but fully resolving -> grade 2. grade_provisional

SPINRAZA label gives the sodium salt as C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17, which is the same molecule (17 H replaced by 17 Na). Sequence reproduces existing row OLG004 character-for-character - used as a parser-validation target. ;; [regulatory] Uniformly modified 2'-MOE phosphorothioate ASO, 18 nucleotide residues, printed in EMA EPAR EMA/289068/2017 sec 2.2.2 as 5'-MeU MeC A MeC MeU MeU MeU MeC A MeU A A MeU G MeC MeU G G-3'; same document states 17 phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages. All residues MOE-modified so all uppercase. Equivalent DNA-base rendering TCACTTTCATAATGCTGG. Molecular formula C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17, MW 7501.0 Da (FDA label sec 11). Two approved IT regimens: 12 mg loading/12 mg maintenance (Low Dose Regimen) and 50 mg loading/28 mg maintenance (High Dose Regimen). ;; [hydrocephalus] Uniformly 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl)-modified, fully phosphorothioate 18-mer splice-switching ASO; no DNA gap, so gapmer_design=NA. Sequence transcribed by the curator from the WHO INN systematic chemical name in the locally held INN List 74 PDF (all residues 2'-MOE, so entire sequence uppercase per the contract's case convention). Approved doses: 12 mg (original regimen) and the higher 50 mg loading / 28 mg maintenance regimen. ;; [clinicaltrials] Label section 11 states verbatim: modified antisense oligonucleotide where the 2'-hydroxy groups of the ribofuranosyl rings are replaced with 2'-O-2-methoxyethyl groups and the phosphate linkages are replaced with phosphorothioate linkages; binds a sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 transcript. Uniformly 2'-MOE modified, therefore gapmer_design=NA and oligo_class=splice_switching_ASO. Length and PS count not stated in the label, so TBD. Label also documents three strengths (12/28/50 mg per 5 mL), which matches the dose arms extracted from NCT04089566. ;; [clinical_programs] Splice-switching ASO that modifies SMN2 pre-mRNA splicing to increase full-length SMN protein. Design fields left TBD because no fetched document in this session printed the chemistry or sequence; the label lane should carry those. ;; [dose_contrast_atlas] [dose_contrast_atlas] Name given EXACTLY as 'nusinersen' so the assembler merges this into the existing CNS012 entry rather than creating a duplicate. Every design field here was read out of the label SPL fetched this session (DailyMed setid dd70cd5f-b0fc-4ba4-a5ea-89a34778bd94, version 21, effectiveTime 20260331). Section 11 DESCRIPTION states verbatim: 'Nusinersen is a modified antisense oligonucleotide, where the 2'-hydroxy groups of the ribofuranosyl rings are replaced with 2'-O-2-methoxyethyl groups and the phosphate linkages are replaced with phosphorothioate linkages. Nusinersen binds to a specific sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 transcript.' Uniform 2'-MOE with no DNA gap -> gapmer_design=NA, oligo_class=splice_switching_ASO. length_nt=18 and ps_count=17 are ARITHMETIC from the molecular formula printed in the same section, C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17: P17 = 17 internucleotide linkages = 18 nucleotides; S17 = 17 phosphorothioates = every linkage, hence full_PS. MW 7501.0 daltons. These are derived from a fetched document, not recalled. sequence_5to3=TBD because section 11 renders the structure only as a 'Structural Formula' image and prints no base string; the existing CNS012 row already carries the sequence from the WHO INN list and EMA EPAR and should be preferred on merge. THE LABEL NOW CARRIES TWO APPROVED REGIMENS (Table 1, sec 2.1): Low Dose Regimen = four 12 mg loading doses (three at 14-day intervals, fourth 30 days later) then 12 mg every 4 months; High Dose Regimen = two 50 mg loading doses 14 days apart then 28 mg every 4 months. Clinical dose in the review: 12 mg IT. ;; [hydro_baseline] ASSEMBLER: merge into the already-curated nusinersen entry (hydrocephalus lane CNS012) and take design metadata from there. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. 4-month-old female with Type I SMA. Findings: enlarging head size and lethargy; communicating hydrocephalus; CSF sample showed no evidence of infection. Management: ventriculo-peritoneal shunt placed; nusinersen continued. Single spontaneously reported case, confounded by underlying SMA (which itself carries ~4-5x baseline hydrocephalus risk) and by repeated lumbar puncture. VPS required - hydrocephalus requiring intervention. ;; corrected: redistribution public_domain -> verify; a Direct Healthcare Professional Communication is issued by the marketing authorisation holder, not by the regulator, so it is not a government work

notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. Verbatim: 'During the reporting period, 9 events pertaining to high-level group term Increased intracranial pressure and hydrocephalus were received in 9 case reports (6 initial and 3 follow-up cases), comprising 9 healthcare professional-confirmed events. All 9 events were considered serious.' The same document states hydrocephalus is an IMPORTANT POTENTIAL RISK in the RMP (not an important identified risk), and that 'a concern on the safety of the higher loading regimen and the potential for patients to develop increased intracranial hypertension (e.g., hydrocephalus) cannot be excluded and is a matter of concern'; the MAH was required to provide a cumulative review of all hydrocephalus cases. Dose is TBD because the 9 spontaneous reports are not attributed to a specific regimen. DO NOT pair this numerator with the '571 participants exposed in interventional clinical studies' figure elsewhere in the same report - that denominator refers to clinical studies, not to the spontaneous reporting stream. ;; VERIFIED[REFUTED] The quoted sentence is verbatim-exact at the cited locus. Two serious problems. (1) readout_name='hydrocephalus_incidence' with readout_value=9 misrepresents what was counted. The source says the 9 events pertain to the HIGH-LEVEL GROUP TER

Retrospective single-centre study of 34 SMA type 1-3 patients on nusinersen; lumbar puncture opening pressure (LOP) measured at treatment lumbar punctures. Numbers read from the PubMed abstract (Results) - the full Thieme text is paywalled and was not fetched, so source_table is the abstract. 12/34 = 35.3%, internally consistent. A markedly raised opening pressure (>=28 cmH2O) in a third of the cohort, yet none symptomatic. Graded 1 (isolated laboratory/physiological abnormality, no functional deficit) rather than 2, because a raised opening pressure without symptoms, papilloedema or imaging change does not meet the grade-2 definition of a clinically significant neurologic adverse event. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. THE MOST IMPORTANT NEGATIVE ROW IN THIS LANE AND ALSO THE WEAKEST - READ THE CAVEAT. This is the largest published survey of neurological findings after intrathecal ASO dosing in non-human primates (28 studies, 1,016 animals). The five sign categories the authors report are: (1) non-adverse transient absence of lower spinal reflexes, dose-related, resolving by 24-48 h; (2) adverse muscle tremor/spasticity during or immediately after injection (one third responded to diazepam, two thirds required euthanasia); (3) ataxia, paresis, nystagmus, urinary incontinence or tremor 30 min to 4 h after dosing; (4) rapidly progressing hind-limb paralysis from spinal cord injury, with MRI-confirmed focal spinal cord necrosis; (5) rare adverse hind-limb paresis or paralysis 2-18 days after dosing. Hydrocephalus, ventriculomegaly and raised intracranial pressure are absent from all five. CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: this is a survey of CLINICAL NEUROLOGICAL SIGNS, not of ventricular imaging or morphometry. The paper does not state that ventricular size was measured, and a monkey with mild ventriculomegaly would very likely show no clinical sign at all. readout_value '0_of_1016' therefore means 'no hydrocephalus reported among the clinical signs in 1,016 animals', NOT 'ventricular size was measured in 1,016 animals and found normal'. Treat as weak negative evidence only. Only the abstract was retrievable. ;; VERIFIED[REFUTED] The descriptive content is exact - 28 intrathecal ASO studies, 1,016 cynomolgus monkeys, and all five sign categories are reproduced faithfully, including the euthanasia outcomes. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. 21-year-old male, 5q SMA (homozygous SMN1 exon 7-8 deletion, 3 SMN2 copies), symptomatic intracranial hypertension the day after his 12th nusinersen injection. Treated with repeated therapeutic lumbar punctures (40, 30, 25, 20 mL removed) and acetazolamide escalated to 2 x 750 mg daily; opening pressure normalised to 23 cmH2O by day 40. SEVERE CONFOUNDING - the paper's own position: the patient had 'extensive, most likely congenital, bilateral arachnoid cysts with moderate space-occupying effects' AND 'bilateral stenosis of the transverse sinuses', either of which can independently cause intracranial hypertension. The authors conclude only that 'the treatment potentially contributed'. Dose: the paper states 5 mL per injection; 5 mL is the 12 mg approved strength (2.4 mg/mL), so 12 mg is recorded here with that derivation made explicit rather than read directly as a mg figure. notes_measurement: [clinicaltrials] n_of_N=21/84. arm=Nusinersen. control arm = Sham Procedure. PROCEDURE-RELATED. Zero back-pain events in the sham arm is exactly what a needle-prick sham predicts. IMPORTANT CONFOUND: the control was a SHAM PROCEDURE - per the study record, 'small needle prick on the lower back at the location where the IT injection is normally made' - NOT a real lumbar puncture. The control arm therefore had no dural puncture, no CSF removal and no intrathecal volume load, so any excess in the nusinersen arm reflects the LUMBAR PUNCTURE PROCEDURE as much as the oligonucleotide. Graded conservatively for that reason. grade_provisional ;; corrected: reversibility -> not_assessed. This is an adverse-event INCIDENCE locus, which reports counts and carries no outcome field; 'did not lead to discontinuation' and 'mild or moderate' are not reversibility

Sequence reproduces existing row OLG004 character-for-character - used as a parser-validation target. ;; [regulatory] Uniformly modified 2'-MOE phosphorothioate ASO, 18 nucleotide residues, printed in EMA EPAR EMA/289068/2017 sec 2.2.2 as 5'-MeU MeC A MeC MeU MeU MeU MeC A MeU A A MeU G MeC MeU G G-3'; same document states 17 phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages. notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. GEN-EXTEND (NCT03842969), tominersen 120 mg Q16W WITHOUT a loading dose. Full printed series of mean % change from baseline: -0.05 (wk17, n=46), -3.42 (wk33, n=40), -1.49 (wk49, n=37), -8.33 (wk66, n=23), -3.76 (wk81, n=10); the recorded value is the maximum reduction. CSF NfL stayed at or BELOW baseline at every timepoint - NO treatment-emergent rise -> grade 0, effect_direction=decrease. This directly contrasts with the Q8W-with-loading rise in GENERATION HD1 and is the strongest evidence in this lane that the tominersen NfL signal is exposure-driven rather than mechanism-obligate.

All events but one resolved - spontaneously, with dosing interruption or modification, or with concomitant therapy; one was ongoing but improved as of December 2022. Raised CSF opening pressure with papilledema/intracranial hypertension in participant 10, with recurrent bitemporal and bioccipital headaches, after 9 doses. KEY NEGATIVE FOR THE HYDROCEPHALUS QUESTION: the paper states explicitly that there was NO imaging evidence of hydrocephalus in any of these participants, 'as distinguished from what has been described with other intrathecal ASOs', while raising the possibility of a non-inflammatory mechanism such as CSF outflow obstruction. Clinical features: rapidly progressive weakness, numbness, pain, loss of ambulation; reported as neurosarcoidosis in a participant with pre-existing systemic sarcoidosis, quiescent at enrolment apart from uveitis. CSF at the event: WBC 44 (77% lymphocytes, 23% monocytes) rising to 88 after 5 days cells/uL, protein 93 rising to 150 after 5 days mg/dL. Baseline CSF protein 38 mg/dL. CSF opening pressure during the event: not measured/not reported. Action taken with tofersen: continued for about 6 months then discontinued. All events in this series resolved except one that was ongoing but improved; none was life-threatening or fatal. The grade on this row is for the PLEOCYTOSIS ITSELF, which is moderate in every case; the severity of the accompanying clinical event is graded on the separate clinical-outcome rows. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:40017137; doi:10.1002/mus.28372

Clinical features: rapidly progressive weakness, numbness, pain and LOSS OF AMBULATION; investigator causality recorded as Unrelated and reported as neurosarcoidosis in a participant with pre-existing systemic sarcoidosis that was quiescent at enrolment apart from uveitis. The authors include the case for completeness given the other myelitis cases in the programme. Action taken: tofersen continued for about 6 months then discontinued. Graded 3 rather than 2 because these are the two events in the whole tofersen serious-neurologic series with a major persisting motor deficit at onset (loss of ambulation; paraplegia) AND both ended in permanent discontinuation of tofersen. Treatment across the myelitis cases included intravenous methylprednisolone with an oral taper, plasma exchange, mycophenolate mofetil and TNF-alpha monoclonal antibody therapy. notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. 56-year-old man with SOD1 c.341T>C p.(Ile114Thr), German tofersen early-access programme. Baseline CSF before treatment was unremarkable (normal protein, cell count, IgG, no oligoclonal bands). Injections 1-5 (days 1, 14, 28, 55, 84) were uneventful. Three days after the 6th injection (day 112; CSF that day 56 cells/uL, total protein 79 mg/dL, oligoclonal bands now positive) he developed generalised myalgia and restless legs, then progressive lower-limb paresis by days 122-124. MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine on day 126 showed low, partly punctiform contrast uptake and oedema consistent with myelitis; CSF then showed 37 cells/uL (lymphocytic), protein 119 mg/dL, CSF/blood IgM quotient 67.2 and positive CSF-specific oligoclonal bands; multiplex PCR for viral and bacterial agents was negative. Treated with intravenous prednisolone 1000 mg/day for 5 days (days 126-131) then an oral taper over 40 days: sensory symptoms and restless legs regressed rapidly but LEG WEAKNESS REGRESSED MUCH MORE SLOWLY -> partially_reversible. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:38066205; doi:10.1007/s00415-023-12130-1

notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. THE DOSE-LIMITING NEUROTOXICITY ROW FOR THIS PROGRAMME. In the PRECISION-HD2 32 mg treatment group alone, seven of thirteen patients reported a serious adverse event - amnesia, ataxia, delirium, disorientation and slurred speech. The events were transient but led six of the thirteen to DISCONTINUE treatment. Graded 3 under the rubric clause 'dose-limiting or programme-halting neurotoxicity', even though the individual events resolved. SEPARATION OF CAUSES: the PROGRAMME was halted in early 2021 because of failure to consistently lower CSF mutant HTT (a target-engagement/futility decision) - the 32 mg escalation was independently limited by these neurologic serious adverse events, which the review says 'raised concerns about the underlying safety and tolerability of the platform'. notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 1, a girl aged 3 at study initiation with KCNT1 p.R474H epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 6, then maintenance 40 mg every 8 weeks from week 10, INCREASED TO 60 mg every 8 weeks from week 26. Eight weeks after her 9th intrathecal dose she developed vomiting and apparent discomfort; brain and spine imaging two days later revealed SEVERE COMMUNICATING HYDROCEPHALUS with T2 white-matter change representing transependymal flow but no other parenchymal change. She was at her baseline alertness with normal pupils, normal extraocular movements, no sunset eye sign and normal vital signs. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy with choroid plexus cauterisation showed a CSF OPENING PRESSURE OF 55 cm H2O and produced no improvement over the following two days. After considering a ventriculoperitoneal shunt, the family withdrew from the investigational protocol in favour of palliative care; she died under hospice care three months after the final ASO dose. GRADE 3: hydrocephalus requiring intervention, with a fatal outcome. notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 2, also a girl aged 3 with KCNT1 p.R474H, enrolled 9 months after patient 1 and about 2 months before hydrocephalus was detected in patient 1. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg. Brain MRI on day 55 was UNREMARKABLE with normal ventricular size and a normal lumbar opening pressure of 16 cm H2O; repeat MRIs on days 62 and 64 showed MILD INCREASES IN VENTRICULAR SIZE with no evidence of obstruction. Given the finding in patient 1 she was transferred to intensive care for neurologic monitoring, an extraventricular drain was placed (opening pressure >20 cm H2O), drainage was persistent, and a VENTRICULOPERITONEAL SHUNT WAS PLACED ON DAY 65. Ventricular dilatation gradually normalised on serial MR ventriculograms and she was discharged home in stable condition on day 87. exposure_duration: every 4 months for up to 36 months
notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. SWALLOWTAIL (NCT04740476) and LONGWING (ISRCTN12811235) open-label extensions: 75 of the 81 phase 1-2a patients entered and continued to receive zorevunersen at up to 45 mg every 4 months. An ELEVATED CSF PROTEIN LEVEL was the commonest adverse event in the extensions, in 45% of patients - i.e. it emerged as the dominant finding only on chronic dosing, which is exactly the chronic-neurotoxicity signal this dataset is built around. Graded 1 (isolated CSF-protein elevation with no stated clinical sequelae), but this is the most under-characterised chronic CNS signal in this lane: the abstract does not say whether the elevations were persistent, progressive, or accompanied by pleocytosis, and this row should be re-extracted from the full text. Read from the abstract. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:41780062; doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2506295

notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. Consortium-level restatement of the valeriasen experience by the N=1 Collaborative: 'Initially valeriasen was effective at reducing seizure activity in Valeria and a second patient whose treatment commenced after Valeria. Unexpectedly, the ASO resulted in the development of hydrocephalus in both patients. This adverse effect had not been observed in safety studies conducted in healthy rats, but was hypothesized to be specifically due to the pathological state of the human brain.' THIS IS THE KEY TRANSLATIONAL POINT FOR THIS DATASET - a CNS toxicity that healthy-rodent toxicology did not predict, which is precisely the predictive gap the OligoTox challenge is aimed at. The review adds that hydrocephalus and inflammation have been reported with other ASOs and calls for safety-data sharing. This row intentionally DUPLICATES the two primary Nature Medicine patient rows in order to preserve the consortium framing; de-duplicate against the primary source at assembly if only one representation is wanted. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:40277082; doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf346

notes_oligo: [sequences] Uniformly 2'-MOE, no DNA gap (splice-switching, targets SMN2 intron 7 ISS-N1). INN List 74 formula C234H340N61O128P17S17 -> P17 = 18 nt, S17 = 17 PS = fully phosphorothioate. SPINRAZA label gives the sodium salt as C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17, which is the same molecule (17 H replaced by 17 Na). Sequence reproduces existing row OLG004 character-for-character - used as a parser-validation target. ;; [regulatory] Uniformly modified 2'-MOE phosphorothioate ASO, 18 nucleotide residues, printed in EMA EPAR EMA/289068/2017 sec 2.2.2 as 5'-MeU MeC A MeC MeU MeU MeU MeC A MeU A A MeU G MeC MeU G G-3'; same document states 17 phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages. The paper does not print the nucleotide sequence, wing/gap lengths or overall length, so sequence_5to3, length_nt, gapmer_design and ps_count are TBD.
effect_vs_control: 2/4 at 1 mg/animal vs 1/4 in the concurrent aCSF control group
source_table: Table 1 (microscopic observations), brain rows; narrative in sections 3.14.1 and 3.14.3
notes_measurement: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; incidence pooled across the 2 males and 2 females examined at each dose level (severity graded minimal/slight/moderate; counted here as present vs not present). Tissue: brain. 13-week GLP toxicity study in cynomolgus monkeys (2 males + 2 females per dose group, so n=4 per dose). aCSF vehicle control or 1, 2 or 4 mg NVP-13 per animal given intrathecally at L4/L5 on days 1, 15, 29, 43, 57, 71 and 85 (0.5 mL CSF removed first, 0.75 mL injected over ~1 min, 0.25 mL aCSF flush). A separate recovery group was necropsied after a recovery phase. NOAEL stated as at least 4 mg/animal. Authors' interpretation: mononuclear infiltration occurred at all dose levels with NO dose relationship, was perivascular and mostly meningeal, and was highest at the lumbar cord/injection site; gliosis and slight demyelination were attributed to the dosing procedure rather than the test item; minimal DRG neuronolysis was seen in a few treated animals but also in a recovery control and is known to occur spontaneously. Recovery-group necropsy showed the same pattern of CNS changes but with generally lower incidence and/or intensity, which the authors interpret as ongoing recovery - hence partially_reversible. ;; source_ref_as_cited=doi:10.3390/pharmaceutics14010200; PMID 35057094; PMC8780845 ;; redistribution_upgraded_to_cc_by_from_archived_licence_statement

Sequence reproduces existing row OLG004 character-for-character - used as a parser-validation target. ;; [regulatory] Uniformly modified 2'-MOE phosphorothioate ASO, 18 nucleotide residues, printed in EMA EPAR EMA/289068/2017 sec 2.2.2 as 5'-MeU MeC A MeC MeU MeU MeU MeC A MeU A A MeU G MeC MeU G G-3'; same document states 17 phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages. source_table: Pharmacology Review p.38 (PDF p.41), 1-year monkey study, Fluoro-Jade B staining narrative
notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] Recovery sacrifice after 26 weeks off drug. 'Fluoro-Jade B staining conducted on two slides/four full coronal (left) sections (two sections at the level of the hippocampus; up to two sections at the level of the cerebellum/brain stem) of the brain from each animal did not reveal any necrotic neurons in any of the study animals (terminal or recovery sacrifice).' Denominator 0/14 = all animals in the study at that sacrifice were negative; the review does not print a per-group count, and the exact per-group n is therefore not asserted here beyond 'none in any animal'. This is the decisive negative that keeps the chronic hippocampal lesion out of grade 3. NOAEL for this study = 0.3 mg/dose ('The NOAEL was 0.3 mg/dose', Pharmacology Review p.47; 'The no-effect dose (0.3 mg) for neurotoxicity in the 53-week monkey study', supervisory memo p.12). The Executive Summary p.4 gives the monkey neurohistopathology NOAEL as 0.3 mg/dose (39 mg/year). grade_provisional. ;; corrected: reversibility -> not_assessed on a grade-0 row; there is no finding to reverse

source_table: Pharmacology Review p.39 (PDF p.42) Table IVC.8 'Histopathology findings in 1-year monkey study', MALES (Groups 1M-4M); top cell of each pair = terminal sacrifice, bottom cell = recovery sacrifice
notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] Males, terminal Day 372, mean severity 0.20. GRADED 2, NOT 3, ON THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS: 'Fluoro-Jade B staining ... did not reveal any necrotic neurons in any of the study animals (terminal or recovery sacrifice), indicating that the necrotic cells were "most likely not neurons," but the cell type was not determined' (p.38). So this is cellular necrosis in the hippocampus that the study pathologist explicitly declines to call neuronal degeneration - it does not meet the grade-3 bar, unlike the Fluoro-Jade-B-verified necrotic NEURON in the 14-week study. ADVERSITY CALL: the study pathologist judged the vacuolation and very rare necrotic cells 'unlikely to result in any clinical signs or any alteration that would in any way interfere with the animals ability to function normally in its environment'; the FDA reviewer answered 'However, given the apparent neurobehavioral (L & M) changes seen in HD animals, this statement is questionable' (p.38), and the pharm/tox supervisor wrote that the vacuoles 'would not be considered adverse if not accompanied by other microscopic changes, such as necrotic cells or cellular debris' (supervisory memo p.10) - i.e. it is precisely this readout that makes the HD finding adverse. Above the NOAEL of 0.3 mg. Recovery not evaluated in the MD group. GRADED 2, NOT 3, ON THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS: 'Fluoro-Jade B staining ... did not reveal any necrotic neurons in any of the study animals (terminal or recovery sacrifice), indicating that the necrotic cells were "most likely not neurons," but the cell type was not determined' (p.38). So this is cellular necrosis in the hippocampus that the study pathologist explicitly declines to call neuronal degeneration - it does not meet the grade-3 bar, unlike the Fluoro-Jade-B-verified necrotic NEURON in the 14-week study. ADVERSITY CALL: the study pathologist judged the vacuolation and very rare necrotic cells 'unlikely to result in any clinical signs or any alteration that would in any way interfere with the animals ability to function normally in its environment'; the FDA reviewer answered 'However, given the apparent neurobehavioral (L & M) changes seen in HD animals, this statement is questionable' (p.38), and the pharm/tox supervisor wrote that the vacuoles 'would not be considered adverse if not accompanied by other microscopic changes, such as necrotic cells or cellular debris' (supervisory memo p.10) - i.e. it is precisely this readout that makes the HD finding adverse. No necrotic cells or debris in HD females at either timepoint. NOAEL for this study = 0.3 mg/dose ('The NOAEL was 0.3 mg/dose', Pharmacology Review p.47; 'The no-effect dose (0.3 mg) for neurotoxicity in the 53-week monkey study', supervisory memo p.12). notes_measurement: [dose_contrast_atlas] [dose_contrast_atlas] THE ONLY NEUROLOGIC/PROCEDURE-RELATED TERM IN THE ENTIRE HIGH-DOSE ADVERSE-REACTION TABLE. Read from DailyMed SPINRAZA SPL setid dd70cd5f-b0fc-4ba4-a5ea-89a34778bd94, version 21, effectiveTime 20260331 ('Revised: 3/2026'), fetched this session. Denominators are printed in the table header verbatim: 'SPINRAZA High Dose Regimen (Study 4) (N=50)' and 'Matched Sham Control (Study 1) (N=20)'. Dose is the High Dose Regimen, two 50 mg loading doses then 28 mg every 4 months (label Table 1, sec 2.1); dose_or_conc_value is set to the 50 mg loading dose, and the 28 mg maintenance dose is the other half of the same regimen. COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT PRINTED: the label prints percentages only; 6% of 50 = 3 patients and 0% of 20 = 0 patients, so '3/50 vs 0/20' is arithmetic and is marked implied. CONTROL IS NOT CONCURRENT: label sec 6.1 states verbatim that the comparator is 'historic-matched sham-control patients from Study 1', and the Table 4 header labels it 'Matched Sham Control (Study 1)'. Study 1 is NCT02193074 (the 12 mg infantile-onset sham-controlled trial), so the N=20 comparator is a matched SUBSET of that trial's N=41 sham arm - it is a historical external control, and the N=20 and N=41 control groups in this lane are NESTED, not independent. SHAM COMPARATOR CAVEAT: the sham procedure in Study 1 was a skin prick with no dural puncture, so any procedure-attributable event - procedural pain, post-lumbar-puncture headache, back pain - is systematically exaggerated by this comparison, because only the treated arm was actually punctured. Graded conservatively at 1 for that reason: transient, procedure-attributable, no evidence of parenchymal injury. DOSE CONTRAST, BOUNDED: procedural pain does NOT appear in Table 2 (the 12 mg infantile-onset table, N=80 vs sham N=41). That is NOT an incidence of zero - Table 2 lists only reactions occurring in at least 5% of SPINRAZA patients AND at least 5% more frequently or at least 2x as frequently as control, so all that can be said is that procedural pain fell below that threshold at 12 mg in the same population type. Do not read the absence as 0%. PATIENT OVERLAP - DO NOT SUM: Study 4 is NCT04089566 (DEVOTE) Part B, and its n=50 infantile-onset high-dose patients are the SAME 50 patients already represented in this dataset by CMS1304 (acquired_macrocephaly 1/50) from NCT04089566 and by CMS1589/CMS1597/CMS1600/CMS1603 from doi:10.1038/s41591-025-04193-6. This row adds a new endpoint on that cohort, not new patients. grade_provisional

This is the high-dose counterpart of the existing CMS1175 (which anchors the 12 mg infantile-onset Table 2) and is NEW - no existing row covers Table 4. Read from DailyMed SPINRAZA SPL setid dd70cd5f-b0fc-4ba4-a5ea-89a34778bd94, version 21, effectiveTime 20260331, fetched this session. Table 4 contains exactly seven rows and they are, in full, with SPINRAZA High Dose Regimen (N=50) percent vs Matched Sham Control from Study 1 (N=20) percent: Pneumonia 20/5, COVID-19 16/0, Pneumonia aspiration 14/5, Malnutrition 10/0, Procedural pain 6/0, Myocardial necrosis marker increased 6/0, Anemia 6/0. Of these only 'Procedural pain' is neurologic or procedure-related (filed separately as TMP_dca_m1); NO central-nervous-system adverse reaction - no headache, no back pain, no post-lumbar-puncture syndrome, no hydrocephalus, no meningitis, no seizure, no papilledema - met the table's reporting threshold at the High Dose Regimen. 'Pneumonia aspiration' is NOT counted as a neurologic event here: aspiration in infantile-onset SMA reflects bulbar weakness from the underlying disease, and the label offers no attribution to nusinersen. IMPORTANT LIMIT ON THIS NEGATIVE: the threshold is 'at least 5% of SPINRAZA High Dose Regimen patients AND at least 5% more frequently or at least 2 times as frequently than matched sham control', so this row establishes only that no neurologic term cleared that bar - it is not a demonstration that neurologic events did not occur. With N=50 a single patient is 2%, so events below roughly 3 patients could not clear the 5% bar at all. Two further limits: the comparator is a historical matched subset of the Study 1 sham arm rather than a concurrent control (label sec 6.1: 'historic-matched sham-control patients from Study 1'), and that sham arm received a skin prick with no dural puncture. notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] Male and female cynomolgus monkeys, 0/4/12/35 mg tofersen IT every 2 weeks for 13 weeks. 'Repeat IT dosing of 0, 4, 12, and 35 mg tofersen every 2 weeks for 13 weeks in male and female cynomolgus monkeys resulted in transient decreases in activity in HDF and neuronal vacuolation at all doses; however, staining with Fluoro Jade did not indicate neuronal degeneration. Vacuolation was not observed after a 13-week recovery period.' REVERSIBILITY IS RECOVERY-GROUP EVIDENCE: lesion present at the end of dosing, ABSENT after a 13-WEEK recovery period -> reversible. GRADE 1, not 2: vacuolation without degeneration and fully reversible; contrast the nusinersen monkey studies where the same lesion persisted through 12 and 26 weeks of recovery and is graded 2 here. Incidence, severity, sex split and CNS region are NOT printed in the Integrated Review (the monkey studies were submitted to the IND and are summarised narratively only) -> readout_value TBD and cns_region recorded as whole_brain rather than invented. NOAEL: 12 mg for the CNS safety-pharmacology endpoint in this 13-week study (Section 13.1.2: 'transient reductions in activity in female cynomolgus monkeys, for which the NOAELs were 1 and 12 mg, respectively'). notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] Male and female cynomolgus monkeys, 0/4/12/35 mg tofersen IT every 2 weeks for 13 weeks. 'Repeat IT dosing of 0, 4, 12, and 35 mg tofersen every 2 weeks for 13 weeks in male and female cynomolgus monkeys resulted in transient decreases in activity in HDF and neuronal vacuolation at all doses; however, staining with Fluoro Jade did not indicate neuronal degeneration. Vacuolation was not observed after a 13-week recovery period.' REVERSIBILITY IS RECOVERY-GROUP EVIDENCE: lesion present at the end of dosing, ABSENT after a 13-WEEK recovery period -> reversible. GRADE 1, not 2: vacuolation without degeneration and fully reversible; contrast the nusinersen monkey studies where the same lesion persisted through 12 and 26 weeks of recovery and is graded 2 here. Incidence, severity, sex split and CNS region are NOT printed in the Integrated Review (the monkey studies were submitted to the IND and are summarised narratively only) -> readout_value TBD and cns_region recorded as whole_brain rather than invented. NOAEL: 12 mg for the CNS safety-pharmacology endpoint in this 13-week study (Section 13.1.2: 'transient reductions in activity in female cynomolgus monkeys, for which the NOAELs were 1 and 12 mg, respectively'). Note the neuronal vacuolation occurred at ALL doses including 4 mg, i.e. below the stated NOAEL, and was therefore not treated by the reviewer as the adverse effect that sets the NOAEL - consistent with 'staining with Fluoro Jade did not indicate neuronal degeneration'. grade_provisional.

'Repeat IT dosing of 0, 4, 12, and 35 mg tofersen every 2 weeks for 13 weeks in male and female cynomolgus monkeys resulted in transient decreases in activity in HDF and neuronal vacuolation at all doses; however, staining with Fluoro Jade did not indicate neuronal degeneration. Vacuolation was not observed after a 13-week recovery period.' REVERSIBILITY IS RECOVERY-GROUP EVIDENCE: lesion present at the end of dosing, ABSENT after a 13-WEEK recovery period -> reversible. GRADE 1, not 2: vacuolation without degeneration and fully reversible; contrast the nusinersen monkey studies where the same lesion persisted through 12 and 26 weeks of recovery and is graded 2 here. Incidence, severity, sex split and CNS region are NOT printed in the Integrated Review (the monkey studies were submitted to the IND and are summarised narratively only) -> readout_value TBD and cns_region recorded as whole_brain rather than invented. NOAEL: 12 mg for the CNS safety-pharmacology endpoint in this 13-week study (Section 13.1.2: 'transient reductions in activity in female cynomolgus monkeys, for which the NOAELs were 1 and 12 mg, respectively'). Note the neuronal vacuolation occurred at ALL doses including 4 mg, i.e. below the stated NOAEL, and was therefore not treated by the reviewer as the adverse effect that sets the NOAEL - consistent with 'staining with Fluoro Jade did not indicate neuronal degeneration'. grade_provisional.

notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] 'vacuolation was not accompanied by neurodegeneration' (p.83). Negative row at the top chronic dose in the longest tofersen animal study. NOAEL: 12 mg every 2 weeks. 'Based on neurological signs in the 9-month study, the NOAEL for IT administration of tofersen in cynomolgus monkey was 12 mg every 2 weeks, resulting in plasma Cmax and AUC0-24h of 4840 ng/mL and 30,000 ug.h/mL, respectively.' (The AUC unit as printed, ug.h/mL alongside a Cmax in ng/mL, looks like a units error in the source; quoted verbatim, not corrected.) The NOAEL was set on the NEUROLOGICAL SIGNS, not on the vacuolation, which occurred at all doses including below the NOAEL. grade_provisional.

notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] Male and female cynomolgus monkeys, 0/4/12/35 mg tofersen IT every 2 weeks for 9 months. 'In monkeys, IT administration of 0, 4, 12, and 35 mg tofersen in male and female cynomolgus monkeys every other week for 9 months resulted in histologic findings of neuronal vacuolation at all doses; however, vacuolation was not accompanied by neurodegeneration and was not present in recovery groups' (p.83). REVERSIBILITY IS RECOVERY-GROUP EVIDENCE: 'was not present in recovery groups'. THE RECOVERY INTERVAL IS NOT STATED anywhere in the Integrated Review for this 9-month study - only for the 13-week study (13 weeks) - so it is not asserted here. Incidence, severity, sex split and CNS region are not printed -> readout_value TBD. GRADE 1: reversible vacuolation without neurodegeneration. NOAEL: 12 mg every 2 weeks. 'Based on neurological signs in the 9-month study, the NOAEL for IT administration of tofersen in cynomolgus monkey was 12 mg every 2 weeks, resulting in plasma Cmax and AUC0-24h of 4840 ng/mL and 30,000 ug.h/mL, respectively.' (The AUC unit as printed, ug.h/mL alongside a Cmax in ng/mL, looks like a units error in the source; quoted verbatim, not corrected.) The NOAEL was set on the NEUROLOGICAL SIGNS, not on the vacuolation, which occurred at all doses including below the NOAEL. grade_provisional.

notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] 'Four of one hundred forty-seven participants (2.7%) who received 100 mg tofersen in Study 101C or Study 102 reported events of myelitis (preferred terms myelitis, myelitis transverse, and neurosarcoidosis) ... No subject receiving placebo in Study 101C experienced an SAE of myelitis or radiculitis.' Counting note the source itself creates: the Issue paragraph says 'Five subjects receiving tofersen in Studies 101C, 102, AND THE EXPANDED-ACCESS PROGRAM experienced an SAE of myelitis' - 4/147 is the trial-population figure, 5 includes the EAP. Context: 'The incidence of transverse myelitis in the general population is estimated to be approximately 0.0005 to 0.018%. In contrast, 2.7% of subjects ... developed myelitis.' Doses received before onset ranged from 1 to 24. 'Each event was associated with a CSF pleocytosis and elevated CSF protein.' Outcomes were mixed - two cases asymptomatic, one severe case resolved over 2 months, one EAP case of unknown outcome - hence partially_reversible for the aggregate. Reviewer conclusion: 'There is a safety signal for transverse myelitis and radiculitis with intrathecal administration of tofersen.' grade_provisional.

notes_measurement: [fda_reviews] 4/sex/group; vehicle or 10 mg tofersen from one of three impurity-enriched batches (TAM1, TAM2, TAM3), IT Q2W for 13 weeks. 'Histopathology findings consisted of neuronal vacuolation in brain and spinal cord, with no associated degeneration (Fluoro-Jade B staining).' Region split per the dataset grain. This is the ONLY tofersen monkey study in which the review names the affected regions. No incidences printed. No recovery group described -> not_assessed. No NOAEL is stated for this special-purpose study. grade_provisional.

notes_measurement: [hydro_baseline] A GENUINE DRUG-EXPOSURE ROW, AND A DEEPLY CONFOUNDED ONE - READ THE CONFOUND FIRST. In 22 children with type 2/3 SMA, total CSF volume increased significantly after one year of intrathecal nusinersen relative to their own pre-treatment baseline. THERE IS NO UNTREATED-SMA COMPARATOR OVER THE SAME INTERVAL, so this within-subject change cannot be separated from one year of SMA disease progression, and TMP_hb_m28/m29 in this same lane show that untreated SMA already carries elevated CSF volume and impaired glymphatic clearance relative to healthy peers. It also cannot be separated from one year of normal growth in a paediatric cohort. GRADE RATIONALE: grade 2 for a treatment-emergent, statistically significant CNS imaging change; a reviewer could equally justify grade 0 or TBD on the ground that the design cannot attribute it to the drug, and this row should be re-adjudicated at sign-off. readout_value=TBD because the numeric pre/post values live in Supporting Information Tables S2 and S3, which were not retrievable; only the direction and significance were read. Nusinersen dose is not stated in the material fetched, hence dose_or_conc_value/unit=TBD. Lan 2026 (CNS Neurosci Ther 32(8):e71063, CC BY 4.0) prospectively recruited 48 children with type 2 or 3 SMA and 53 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls, and measured glymphatic/CSF function by DTI analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), enlarged perivascular space frequency, and coupling of global BOLD signal with CSF dynamics. A subgroup of 22 patients was re-imaged after one year of intrathecal nusinersen. This is the closest thing in the literature to a CSF-outflow / CSF-clearance measurement made before and after oligonucleotide exposure in humans. grade_provisional. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:42545100; DOI:10.1002/cns.71063

oligo_name: Hnrnph2 ASO (ASO1, Ionis/St. Jude murine Hnrnph2 gapmer)
developer: Ionis Pharmaceuticals with St. Jude Children's Research Hospital
design_source: Korff 2026 Sci Transl Med PMID 42018666 / author preprint PMC12637667 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.11.04.686541), Results 'ASO targeting mouse Hnrnph2...' and Fig 1I
notes_oligo: [hydro_baseline] Lead of >450 gapmer ASOs designed against murine Hnrnph2 for RNase H degradation, non-allele-specific. Screened in primary mouse cortical neurons at 20 uM then a 4-point dose-response 1.2-32 uM; top 19 taken into an 8-week in vivo activity/tolerability study. ASO1 knocked down Hnrnph2 mRNA by 96% and raised Hnrnph1 mRNA by 63% (fig S1B, S1C). backbone_chemistry=full_PS is read from the paper's use of an antibody that 'selectively recognizes the phosphorthioate backbone of ASOs' to image this ASO in brain (Fig 1I) - the gap/wing motif, length and sequence are NOT stated in the text fetched and are left TBD rather than inferred.
effect_vs_control: Hnrnph2 ASO did not change hydrocephalus incidence vs control ASO; P209L heterozygous females showed no increase over WT littermates 'regardless of treatment'
source_table: Supplementary fig. S6A (qualitative statement read from Results, section on hydrocephalus)
notes_measurement: [hydro_baseline] PRECLINICAL NEGATIVE - a study that explicitly looked for hydrocephalus after ICV ASO and found no treatment effect. Verbatim from the peer-reviewed abstract: 'Hnrnph2 ASO administration did not alter survival, body weight, or the incidence of hydrocephalus.' Verbatim from the Results: 'Hnrnph2 ASO treatment did not rescue the increased incidence of hydrocephalus in Hnrnph2 P209L hemizygous males (fig. S6A)' and 'Hnrnph2 P209L heterozygous females did not show an increased incidence of hydrocephalus compared to their WT littermates, regardless of treatment (fig. S6A)'. The second sentence is the load-bearing one for toxicology: WT littermates in this experiment received ASO, and neither ASO arm produced excess hydrocephalus. Korff 2026 (Sci Transl Med 18(846):eadx3491) is paywalled and not in PMC; the peer-reviewed abstract was read from PubMed and the dosing, group structure and hydrocephalus text were read from the authors' own preprint deposited in PMC (PMC12637667, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.11.04.686541, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - hence redistribution=summary_stat). Design: >450 gapmer ASOs against murine Hnrnph2 screened in primary mouse cortical neurons at 20 uM and a 1.2-32 uM dose-response; lead ASO1 given by SINGLE BOLUS ICV injection at postnatal day 2-4 in a 1.875-30 ug dose range, of which the authors state 'all doses of control ASO and Hnrnph2 ASO were well tolerated in this cohort' and 30 ug was carried forward into every phenotype study. Hydrocephalus ascertainment in this mouse line, per the authors' earlier phenotyping paper, is by domed head on gross observation or ventricular enlargement on MRI; the exact ascertainment used in fig S6 is not stated in the text fetched. readout_value=TBD because the per-arm counts live only in supplementary fig S6A/S6B, which this curator did not read numerically - the text statement is qualitative. FRAMING CAVEAT THE DATASET MUST NOT LOSE: the study's own framing of this endpoint is EFFICACY (the ASO failed to RESCUE a genotype-driven hydrocephalus phenotype), not toxicology. It is nonetheless a valid grade-0 toxicology row because hydrocephalus was scored in ASO-treated animals and ASO exposure did not raise it. grade_provisional. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:42018666; DOI:10.1126/scitranslmed.adx3491 (dose and per-arm design read from the author-deposited preprint, PMC12637667 / bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2025.11.04.686541)
